stories.title: South Korea's KOSPI drops 4% as chip stocks slide after worst month since 2008
stories.summary: South Korea's KOSPI index fell about 4%, led lower by semiconductor and chip-related names, after Investing.com reported the index just posted its worst month since 2008. The slide underscores mounting pressure on chip stocks in the region.
stories.whyItMatters: South Korea's market is a bellwether for global chip demand, so a concentrated selloff in semiconductor names signals investors reassessing the broader tech/AI trade.
whatToWatch: Whether chip stocks stabilize or the selloff spreads to other Asian tech markets
Any follow-through into US semiconductor names
questions: What specifically triggered the acceleration in chip-stock selling?
Is this a Korea-specific issue or part of a broader tech correction?

stories.whyItMatters: S-Oil's results offer a read on Asian refining margins, relevant for energy investors and anyone tracking oil-product demand.

Any guidance on capital spending or dividends

stories.title: About 60,000 evacuated as wildfires threaten Spokane, Washington
stories.summary: Roughly 60,000 people have been ordered to evacuate as wildfires spread near Spokane, Washington, according to Investing.com. The scale of the order points to a fast-moving and significant fire threat in the area.
stories.whyItMatters: Large wildfires can disrupt regional infrastructure and property markets, with knock-on effects for insurers and West Coast utilities that investors track.
whatToWatch: Containment progress and whether evacuation orders expand or are lifted
Any impact on regional power infrastructure or insurers
questions: What caused the fires?
How many structures or how much acreage is affected?

stories.title: Worley wins engineering contract for Missouri cobalt refinery
stories.summary: Engineering firm Worley has been awarded a contract to provide engineering services for a cobalt refinery project in Missouri, per Investing.com. Cobalt is a key battery input, making refinery buildouts a point of interest for critical-minerals supply chains.
stories.whyItMatters: New domestic cobalt refining capacity feeds into efforts to build out US battery and EV supply chains outside Chinese-dominated processing.
whatToWatch: Timeline and scale details on the Missouri refinery as they emerge
Which company owns or will operate the refinery Worley is engineering for
questions: Who is the refinery's owner/operator and what is its expected capacity?
What is the contract's value and timeline?

stories.whyItMatters: Escalation or de-escalation in the conflict remains a factor markets watch for oil-price moves and broader risk sentiment.
whatToWatch: Any ceasefire or deal announcements
Reaction in oil prices tied to Middle East risk
questions: What would need to change for a deal to be reached?
Is this pace of strikes an escalation from prior weeks?

stories.title: Australia's Steadfast jumps after consortium reaffirms $5.4 billion takeover offer
stories.summary: Shares of Australian insurance broker group Steadfast rose after a consortium reaffirmed its $5.4 billion takeover offer, according to Investing.com. The reaffirmation removes some uncertainty about whether the deal remains on the table.
stories.whyItMatters: A confirmed multi-billion-dollar buyout signals continued private-capital appetite for insurance-distribution assets and is a re-rating event for shareholders.
whatToWatch: Formal deal terms, financing, and any regulatory approval steps
Steadfast board's response and shareholder vote timeline
questions: Who are the members of the consortium?
Has a firm price per share been set, or is $5.4 billion still indicative?

stories.summary: The Japanese yen strengthened as traders positioned for possible further currency intervention, according to Investing.com. The move follows a stretch of yen weakness that has previously prompted official action.
stories.whyItMatters: Japanese intervention risk affects global FX positioning and carry trades, and can ripple into US Treasury yields given Japan's large holdings.
whatToWatch: Any confirmed intervention by Japanese authorities
USD/JPY levels relative to prior intervention thresholds
questions: What level would trigger actual intervention this time?
Are officials signaling verbally or is this purely market positioning?

stories.title: S-Oil Q2 2026 slides show lube profit surging as refining normalizes
stories.summary: Slides from S-Oil's Q2 2026 earnings presentation show its lubricants business posting a sharp profit increase even as broader refining conditions normalize, per Investing.com. The materials point to lubricants as a standout contributor to the quarter.
stories.whyItMatters: A strong lube segment alongside normalizing refining margins suggests S-Oil's earnings mix is diversifying, a detail refining-sector investors will want to track.

Segment-level guidance from S-Oil for coming quarters
questions: What is driving the surge in lube profit specifically?

stories.whyItMatters: China's factory health feeds directly into global commodity demand, trade flows, and multinational earnings, making PMI readings a closely watched macro signal.
whatToWatch: Official China PMI data for confirmation or divergence
Any policy response from Beijing if softness persists
questions: How does this reading compare with the prior month's level?
